flashcard_questions.q: At which siege did Paré run out of boiling oil?
What did Paré use silk ligatures for during amputation?
flashcard_questions.a: Tying off blood vessels to control bleeding.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does war speed up medical progress?
flashcard_questions.a: Thousands of wounded create an urgency that peacetime medicine never faces.

flashcard_questions.q: In which war did Florence Nightingale reform military hospitals?
How far did Nightingale’s reforms cut the death rate at Scutari?
Which nursing school did Nightingale found in 1860?
flashcard_questions.a: The Nightingale Training School at St Thomas’ Hospital.

flashcard_questions.q: What were the “petites Curies” of World War One?
flashcard_questions.a: Mobile X-ray units mounted in vehicles near the front.

flashcard_questions.q: Who identified the blood groups in 1901?
In which year did the first blood banks appear?
Which surgeon pioneered plastic surgery for facial injuries in World War One?

flashcard_questions.a: Running an antiseptic solution through wounds using tubes.
